title: The Half-Life Illusion
dek: AI benchmarks are saturating more than five times faster than a decade ago — but only when a problem comes with a clean answer key. Open-world agency, frontier research, and a widening open-weight moat tell a far sharper story.
byline: Visual Essay · Epoch AI, Artificial Analysis, SWE-bench & METR (2016–2026)
sourceNote: Sources: Epoch AI Capabilities & Benchmarking Hub (69 bounded benchmarks normalized on [random, 100%], 1,282 models, Nov 2026); Artificial Analysis Models Leaderboard (290 live models); SWE-bench Official Leaderboards; METR Time Horizons v1.1.

beats.headline: Saturated benchmarks are dying over 5× faster — even before 2026

bodySegments.text: Across 69 bounded evaluations in Epoch AI's hub,
classic 2016–2020 milestones
survived a median 69.6 months before crossing 85% of the range to perfection. For
post-2020 saturated benchmarks
, that lifespan shrank to 22.9 months (2021–23) and 13.0 months in 2024–25 (5.4× faster; 4.3m including 2026) — yet 38 tests in the top band remain unbroken.

beats.headline: In 2026, four new tests arrived already saturated

bodySegments.text: Zooming into the 53 tests launched since 2024 shows both speed and right-censoring: 32 remain open, while
the 21 that fell collapsed fast
— ARC-AGI-2 in 13.0 months, ProofBench in 4.3, MirrorCode in 0.9. Four 2026 releases —
FrontierMath Tiers 1–3 v2, FrontierMath Tier-4 v2, Surface Evolver, and DTBench
— crossed 85% on models released before publication.

beats.takeaway: 4 tests in 2026 arrived pre-saturated; 32 of 53 post-2024 remain open.

beats.headline: AI isn't breaking every test — only the ones with an answer key

bodySegments.text: Grouping all 69 benchmarks by task structure reveals a sharp fault line (pre-2024 tests faded). Among 2024–2026 releases,
verifiable math, coding & puzzles
reach an 88.0% median peak (12 of 21 saturated), and
knowledge & STEM QA
sits at 85.7% (5 of 10). Meanwhile,
agentic & open-world tasks
stall at 69.1%, with just 4 of 22 (18%) crossing 85%.

beats.chartSubtitle: Peak frontier score by domain (2024–26 bold)

beats.headline: Open-world agency and frontier research still resist saturation

bodySegments.text: Coding agents surged —
SWE-bench Verified
jumped from 0.4% to 79.2% (83.5% on Epoch AI), while METR's task horizon doubled every 129 days since 2023 (188d all-time). Past 12 months,
stubborn agency & research holdouts
endure — ForecastBench (33.2%), Agent Co. (42.9%), Remote Labor (41.2%), HLE (52.5%), CritPt (36.0%), plus 2026 entrant CL-bench (27.9%).

beats.takeaway: Past 12m, forecasting, workplace agency & research QA resist saturation.

beats.headline: Open weights caught up on old tests — and fell behind on new ones

bodySegments.text: Comparing best closed and open scores flips conventional wisdom.
Pre-2024 tests hug the parity line
(median closed lead +0.0 pp in 2016–20, +1.7 pp in 2021–23). On 2024–26 tests, dots plunge into the
proprietary moat below the diagonal
— +32.3 pp on Terminal Bench (35 open models), +55.4 pp on ExploitBench, and +61.0 pp on EBR-bench (*Cybench/GSO also reflect sparse open testing).

beats.takeaway: Median closed lead jumped from +1.7pp (2021–23) to +16.8pp (2024–26).

beats.headline: Artificial Analysis confirms the widening reasoning moat

bodySegments.text: Within Epoch's 2024–26 cohort, median closed leads hit
+23.1 pp on agentic
and +16.8 pp on verifiable tasks (vs. +12.1 pp on QA). Artificial Analysis's standardized 290-model leaderboard rules out sparse-testing bias:
GPQA (+0.6 pp) and TerminalBench-Hard (+9.1 pp)
stay tight, while
CritPt v2 Hard (+27.0 pp) and HLE-Diamond (+42.9 pp)
drive an 18.2-point Intelligence Index chasm (64.8 vs. 46.6).

beats.takeaway: Artificial Analysis (290 models): GPQA +0.6pp, TerminalBench-Hard +9.1pp, HLE-Diamond +42.9pp.
